pull_request.title: Add resilient payment retry lifecycle
pull_request.body: Introduces explicit payment states and guarded retry transitions so duplicate webhooks cannot charge a customer twice.
pull_request.author: demo-engineer

changed_files.patch:
+class PaymentState:
+    PENDING = 'pending'
+    PROCESSING = 'processing'
+    RETRY_WAIT = 'retry_wait'
+    SUCCEEDED = 'succeeded'
+    FAILED = 'failed'

+if payment.state == RETRY_WAIT and retry_due(payment):
+    payment.transition_to(PROCESSING)
+    gateway.charge(payment.idempotency_key)

diagram.title: Resilient payment retry lifecycle
diagram.selection_reason: The feature is governed by explicit payment states and guarded transitions.
diagram.summary: A payment starts pending, moves into processing, and either succeeds, fails permanently, or waits before retrying. Duplicate provider webhooks are ignored, and the same idempotency key is reused so a retry cannot create a second charge.

evidence.description: Defines the five payment lifecycle states.
evidence.excerpt: PENDING → PROCESSING → RETRY_WAIT, SUCCEEDED, or FAILED

evidence.description: Moves due retries back to processing and reuses the idempotency key.
Ignores provider events that have already been processed.

memories.title: Retries must reuse the original idempotency key
memories.relevance: Explains why retrying a timed-out request cannot create a second charge.
memories.narrative: A previous incident showed that generating a new key during retry could create duplicate provider charges.

memories.title: Stripe webhooks are delivered at least once
memories.relevance: Explains the processed-event guard in the webhook handler.
memories.narrative: Webhook delivery may repeat after a timeout, so handlers must be idempotent.

greptile.summary: The PR adds a payment state model, retry transitions, and duplicate webhook protection.
review_comments: Retry attempts preserve the original payment idempotency key.
Processed provider event IDs prevent duplicate state transitions.
